scope.population: 2,480,267 row-aligned fills; every net figure is measured on the 1,234,777 LATE-half fills, and the toxic cut is the top 10% of the 2,069 takers with at least 50 early fills, which is 207 wallets
scope.window: single December window; early days [4, 5, 6, 7, 8], late days [9, 10, 11, 12, 13]
scope.note: computed entirely on-disk from the two intermediates; no S3 re-pull. env_slice says whether CAP_DAYS or CAP_COINS narrowed the population for a smoke run, which is the one thing that would make the counts above describe less than the whole input

declared_not_confirmed.note: settings.py declares these; this run did not state what it used, so they are the declaration and not a property of this artifact

override_reasons.master_seed: the streams here are seeded 20260621, not the declared 20260620; settings.MASTER_SEED carries the state 'target', so adopting it re-draws every placebo stream and moves the published p-values
override_reasons.n_boot: the run drew 2000 resamples, which IS the declared 2000: stated as a CONFIRMATION and not as a deviation. It was 1000 until 2026-07-31, half the declaration, so every confidence interval in this file moved with the adoption and no point estimate did
override_reasons.rank_floor_fills: the headline cell gates takers at 50 early fills, which IS the declared 50: a CONFIRMATION and not a deviation. It was 10 until 2026-07-31, and this file was one of the four reasons the declaration stood as a target. The reported sweep is [1, 2, 3, 5, 10, 25, 50, 100] since 2026-08-03 and is WIDER than the declared [10, 50]: four rungs come from settings.RANK_FLOOR_SENSITIVITY and four more ([1, 2, 3, 5]) are declared in maker_econ.py, which is a debt recorded there. The 10-fill arm is the robustness companion

_meta.author: Dmitry Stakhin
_meta.fee_source: Hyperliquid fee schedule fetched 2026-06-21 from the official docs (hyperliquid.gitbook.io/hyperliquid-docs/trading/fees): maker 1.5 bps base -> 1.2/0.8/0.4 -> 0 bps (>$500M 14d vol); maker rebate -0.1/-0.2/-0.3 bps by 14d maker-volume share; taker 4.5 -> 2.4 bps. 1 bp = 0.01%.
_meta.ladder_policy: EIGHT RUNGS ARE PUBLISHED, keyed K<fills>, and they carry different blocks on purpose. Every rung has its label set, its decile table, its B1 gain and a WALLET-CLUSTERED interval on that gain with two whale arms. Only the rungs in k_rungs_with_permutation_null carry the 2000-draw permutation placebo, which is the run's dominant cost at about 136 s per rung and horizon against about 2 s for everything else at that cell, measured 2026-08-03. That is a stated bar and not an omission: the placebo block's observed_toxicity_delta is the same arithmetic as the B1 block's delta_net_vw_bps at the same cell, so a rung without a null still publishes its gain and its interval, and what it does not publish is a p. Before 2026-08-03 only K10 and K50 existed here at all, and the six rungs between and around them were reported in prose from a scratch run whose output never entered the tree. k_rung_declarations says, rung by rung, which declaration puts that floor on the ladder; the four rungs below ten are declared in maker_econ.py itself and that is recorded as a debt.
_meta.label_horizon_policy: LABELS AND MEASUREMENT SHARE ONE HORIZON WITHIN EVERY BLOCK. The hXX key of net_by_toxicity_decile and of b1_idealized_policy_upper_bound means: takers were RANKED on the early-window mean a_mid at XX seconds AND the late-window P&L was MEASURED at XX seconds. No block mixes a ranking horizon with a different measurement horizon. This matters because a mixed block books the gain the shorter measurement shows while charging only the notional the longer screen declines, which overstates how efficient the screen is. Eligibility (at least K early fills with a finite a_mid) is counted at the block's own horizon too, so the eligible and toxic taker sets differ slightly between horizons. baseline_net is symmetric and uses no labels. placebo_random_drop is reported at the anchor horizon only, with that horizon's labels. cross_checks reads only day-based label fields, which do not move with the horizon.
_meta.split_rule: The label and evaluation halves are DERIVED from the days present, by settings.split_early_late: first ceil(n/2) days early, the rest late. They used to be the hardcoded day-of-month tuples (4,5,6,7,8) and (9,10,11,12,13), which are correct only for a window opening on the 4th and closing on the 13th. This input does open on the 4th, so the derived split reproduces those tuples exactly and no number moved.

measures.net_PRINT: -a_print_h (mirror of taker print gain; nets entry spread; INDEPENDENT measure 1; uses quickwin_markouts.npz)
measures.net_MID_lower: s_bbo - a_mid_h, s_bbo = spread_entry_bps/2 (BBO half-spread, LOWER BOUND on maker income; INDEPENDENT measure 2; uses quickwin_markouts_mid.npz)
measures.net_MID_approx: s_approx - a_mid_h = -a_print (wiring tautology, NOT independent; guard only)
measures.s_approx: a_mid_h - a_print_h (mean-unbiased realized half-spread; must exceed s_bbo on average)

_meta.sign_convention: a_mid/a_print positive = maker adverse-selected; maker_net positive = the maker earns net of fees.
_meta.policy_label: B1 = idealized UPPER BOUND (perfect per-counterparty control); fill-aware B2 is future work and bounded above.
_meta.no_repull: computed entirely on-disk from the two npz; no S3 re-pull.
